narrative.h2: On TikTok, the first three seconds decide if there's a fourth

sections.heading: What the algorithm actually rewards
sections.body: TikTok's For You page doesn't care about your video's full duration — it cares about retention curve. The watch-through at 3 seconds and the rewatch rate are the two metrics that decide whether your video stops at 200 views or pushes to 200,000. Which means the conventional MV opening — slow build, atmospheric wide, artist walks in at 0:20 — is algorithmic suicide. The hook has to land before the viewer's thumb gets bored.

sections.heading: The 15-60 second sweet spot, structured
sections.body: Creators who post music on TikTok have converged on a shape: cold-open with the chorus (or the catchiest hook), 5 seconds of visual identity, return to the hook, end on a loop-point that drives a rewatch. 30 seconds total is the most-shared length; 60 is the ceiling before retention falls off. Vertical 9:16 is non-negotiable — letterboxed content gets penalized in the feed.

sections.heading: How Tunee exports for TikTok specifically
sections.body: Pick the TikTok preset and Tunee restructures the cut: chorus-first, vocals up in the first second, hook re-stated at the 15-second mark, loop-friendly final frame. You get 9:16 native (not cropped from 16:9 — re-composed), 1080p, MP4 under TikTok's upload cap, and the audio track exported separately so you can also upload it as a TikTok sound and let creators duet it. Two assets, one generation.
